subject: Optimizer toolkit: incentive structure, batching/cache guidance, and quantization roadmap
messages:
From: Eli Martinez <eli@ellipsis-labs.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Query: Optimize toolkit pricing + quant recommendations for summarization pipeline

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the intro earlier. Ellipsis runs a high-throughput summarization pipeline (long documents -> abstractive summaries) — our production load averages ~50k tokens/day today with spikes to 250k on batch jobs. Latency SLO is 200ms p50 for our interactive preview; cost is the bigger constraint. We attached a short workload spec (Ellipsis_Workload_Specs.pdf).

Two asks:
- Rough pricing and packaging for the Optimize toolkit: batching/cache credits, service/eng advisory, and any pilot credit options.
- Your quantization recommendations (we currently run fp16 on A100s but are open to int8/4-bit to cut costs if quality holds). Any caveats re: hallucination or regressions?

Procurement may join once we start commercial talks (cc'd). Looking for a 3–6 week pilot that demonstrates at least 30% per-token cost reduction without >1–2% drop in ROUGE/BLEU-equivalent metrics.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call this week.

— Eli
Eli Martinez
Head of ML, Ellipsis Labs
eli@ellipsis-labs.com

Attachment: Ellipsis_Workload_Specs.pdf (1 page, high-level ops and token distributions)
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Eli Martinez <eli@ellipsis-labs.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Query: Optimize toolkit pricing + quant recommendations for summarization pipeline

Eli — thanks for the brief and the spec. High level response and a concrete pilot proposal below. Happy to jump on a call Friday.

Quick answers up front:
- Recommend a staged quantization approach: start with int8 using Redwood QuantSuite (production-tested int8 kernels) and A/B compare with an AWQ 4-bit variant for latency-sensitive paths. We typically see 30–45% token-cost reduction with int8 and ~55–70% with well‑tuned 4-bit, though 4-bit may require more eval and guardrails for generation quality.
- Caching: prefix-level KV caching for recurring prompts + result-level short-term cache for preview responses. For interactive preview we set a small TTL (30s–2m) to preserve freshness while increasing cache hit rate on repeated previews.
- Batching: for background batch jobs you can use larger windows (100–200ms) to increase throughput; for interactive preview we target a 25ms max batching window with adaptive batching to preserve p50 latency.

Pilot proposal (3 months) — what we can commit to quickly:
- 30k pilot credits (applied to token charges) + one week of dedicated onboarding with our inference team to set model config and caching policy.
- Technical advisory (2 onsite/remote sprints) from Karthik and the Optimize team to tune quantization, evaluate AWQ 4-bit vs int8 on your testset, and set perf/quality gates.
- Packaging options:
  * Option A — Hosted PAYG: lower up-front, incremental credits, recommended for orgs wanting minimal infra lift.
  * Option B — 12-month Dedicated commit with a 12% commit discount + included advisory hours (best for predictable spend).
  * Option C — Private (VPC) deployment: enterprise packaging with separate pricing; we can provide a dedicated quote.

We can include a conditional additional rebate (8% rebate on committed spend up to 12 months) if we hit the pilot goals you noted: >=30% per-token cost reduction AND <=1.5% quality delta on your eval.

Attachments: Optimizer_Pilot_Proposal.pdf, SOW_Draft.docx

Next steps: if this looks directionally right I can loop in Procurement and send a SOW + DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

--
Redwood Inference — production-first inference platform
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimizer toolkit: incentive structure, batching/cache guidance, and quantization roadmap

Quick internal notes / suggested commercial tweaks before we send to procurement:
- Karthik: good call on staged quant. From an SRE/ops POV we should make the AWQ 4-bit path a gated opt-in: offer it as a "performance rebate" path — i.e., if Ellipsis validates quality on a seeded eval set (we run the eval job) we unlock the 4-bit rebate. That reduces our exposure to regression risk.
- Discount sizing: Camila suggested 12% commit discount + 8% conditional rebate. For a customer this size I propose we increase the pilot credits to 50k and make the initial commit discount 15% if they commit to a 12-month Dedicated band >= $120k ARR equivalent (numbers TBD per SOW). Additional 3% partner discount if they sign marketplace listing in 60 days.
- Risk controls: require a quality gate in the SOW (automated eval harness + rollback policy) — this should be non-negotiable.

If we want to be more aggressive, allow a 18% first-year discount but tie 6% of that to quality/latency milestones (we hold those as rebate credits, not upfront concession).

If we go with the 15% commit + 50k pilot credits + gated AWQ unlock, procurement should have a clean path to sign. Thoughts?

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Consultant, Redwood Inference
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Eli Martinez <eli@ellipsis-labs.com>, procurement <procurement@ellipsis-labs.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-13T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Optimizer toolkit: incentive structure, batching/cache guidance, and quantization roadmap — proposal and next steps

Eli / procurement team — thank you for the quick turnaround. Based on our internal alignment, here's the formal offer we can put on the table:

1) Pilot (3 months)
- 50,000 pilot credits applied to token charges (covers both hosted inference and Optimize advisory work).
- Two onboarding sprints with Karthik and team; evaluation harness run against your supplied testset.
- Access to Redwood Optimize tooling for batching/caching suggestions and automated eval dashboards.

2) Commercial terms (if moving to a 12-month Dedicated commit within 60 days):
- 15% commit discount on list pricing for the first 12 months.
- Performance rebate: additional 8% rebate (credited as account credit) unlocked if pilot goals are met: >=30% per-token cost reduction AND <=1.5% delta on your quality metric measured on our harness.
- AWQ 4-bit pathway: gated unlock — we will only enable 4-bit model serving for production after passing the quality gate; we will provide fallbacks to int8 if regressions occur.
- Marketplace listing incentive: optional 3% extra credit if the customer opts to list Redwood integration in the cloud marketplace within 60 days of signed SOW.

3) Risk & ops controls
- Quality gate and automated rollback policy embedded in SOW.
- SLOs for p50 latency for interactive preview maintained at <=200ms — if we miss this target due to Redwood config, account credit applies to next billing period (detailed in SOW).

4) Next steps
- I will attach the final SOW (SOW_Final_Ellipsis.docx) and a DocuSign envelope for signature: https://app.docusign.com/ELL-2028-042/intro
- Once signed we schedule the onboarding and Karthik will kick off the eval harness.

Eli — does that structure sound acceptable? I can lower the commit threshold if procurement prefers a smaller initial band.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
